findings.evidence: EU retention is now 24 months for all EU accounts, effective 1 September 2026, so the Q3 launch can proceed [D4].
findings.why_it_matters: Draft Amendment B (24 months) is explicitly unsigned and unapproved; relying on it gives the COO the wrong legal retention period for the launch.

findings.evidence: The Board approved the change in January and the operational records are aligned [D11].
findings.why_it_matters: The Board explicitly did not approve Draft Amendment B, and operational records (both the system export and the public trust page) are stale and misaligned with signed Amendment A.

findings.evidence: The Board approved Draft Amendment B in January 2026 [D11].
findings.why_it_matters: D11 explicitly states that the Board did not approve Draft Amendment B and instead delegated signature of the earlier proposed amendment to the Chief Legal Officer.

findings.evidence: All EU accounts, including those opened before 2026, move to 18 months [D3].
findings.why_it_matters: Amendment A applies the 18-month retention period only to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026; accounts opened before that date remain at 12 months.

findings.evidence: The public trust page shows 12 months, which is consistent with the current position for existing accounts [D7]. The sales operations email confirms that 12 months is the number to quote [D12].
findings.why_it_matters: Both the public trust page and the February sales operations email are outdated for post-1 January 2026 accounts and the new Q3 tier; the DPO and internal audit identify the trust page and system export as stale records that should not be relied upon.

findings.evidence: Backups are covered by the 18-month retention period [D8].
findings.why_it_matters: Backups are explicitly out of scope of the Enterprise Data Retention Policy and its EU addenda, and are governed separately by a 35-day retention schedule.

findings.evidence: Proceed with the Q3 launch without updating the system export; the signed amendment controls, so operations can rely on this memo [D3][D9].
findings.why_it_matters: Approving the launch without updating the stale system-of-record configuration and public trust page leaves automated systems and customer-facing guidance enforcing the wrong 12-month retention period.
